Adventure journal / People, native Windows Steam + Classic 53.16

Sources: the original files configured as reference and classic in
data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. No running process is attached.
Steam image PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
  SHA256 205770918fd54c96cbbcf89223ebd449e2e113c7c873ed81177c4511a3450db7
Classic image PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
  SHA256 f35bbaf37aa96f93f95f8a35a9341e6649da46bc29a8650316bfdc2dfc57f3e4

The .c files are actual Ghidra 12.1.4 decompiler output, produced with the
existing DecompileJournalAgreementsPE.java generic PE-manifest interface.
Its agreement_ prefix is only a script symbol label. The assembly, literal
operands, conditional edges and native switch targets are the original PE
source. Embedded trailing jump tables are retained as selectors, not decoded
as executable instructions. This text reconstructs the source grammar and
labels inferred object fields; it is neither inferred C nor a game display
observation. Native unwind extents, image paths and digests are in
pe-functions.tsv; executable extents are in pe-ghidra-functions.tsv.

Complete owner and leaf correspondence, Steam / Classic RVA
  c2110 / c20a0   complete journal renderer and card field consumers
  d1ef0 / d1e80   complete person card description producer
  b92900 / b8f940 generated entity name and unknown civilization fallback
  9bdfb0 / 9bb7e0 religious office owner suffix
  a946e0 / a91760 complete generated person/entity name supplier
  aa3bd0 / aa0c50 creature/caste label, including invalid and fallback paths
  aa4850 / aa18d0 gender possessive (her/his/its)
  75a580 / 757fa0 complete kinship vocabulary and native selector aliases
  bb2f30 / baff70 kinship selector computed for the two historical figures
  bc0f20 / bbdf60 social assessment; computes the reputation scores
  bc360 / bc2f0   complete 31-family reputation caption producer
  8e7310 / 8e4b80 one paragraph -> wrapped string-pointer vector
  8e7440 / 8e4cb0 paragraph vector -> wrapped string-pointer vector
  99a3c0..99a4d3 / 997bf0..997d03 complete gendered office-name leaf
  675670..675907 / 673090..673327 complete relative-time leaf

Card caching and field consumption
  Journal mode selector is 2 (People); the renderer's mode dispatch is
  c2fec/c2f7c. The People vector is journal+0x590, containing PersonCard*.
  Selected card index: journal+0x250. Selected paragraph scroll: +0x260.
  First visible card index: journal+0x2b4. The native expanded-card flag is
  journal+0x278. These remain distinct from Events' fields.

  PersonCard+0x00: historical figure pointer
  PersonCard+0x08: unshortened generated title string
  PersonCard+0x48: native shortened display title string
  PersonCard+0x58: title length
  PersonCard+0x68: vector<string*> wrapped description rows begin
  PersonCard+0x70: wrapped description rows end
  PersonCard+0x78: wrapped description rows capacity
  PersonCard+0x80: optional knowledge record used for race/deity/force type

  d1ef0 is called for visible cards each render, but d1f4d returns immediately
  when the +0x68 vector already has rows. It is a cached source. If the title
  length is zero the producer copies the +0x08 name and shortens the display
  title with width 58. Each independently emitted description paragraph adds an
  empty string row first when preceding rows exist, then uses width 58.

  Title addst return c8a0d/c899d reads card+0x48.
  Counter addst return c8ab3/c8a43 is one-based index / total.
  Paragraph addst return c8b77/c8b07 reads +0x68[scroll+line].
  The paragraph line cursor is set at c8b52/c8ae2. For the selected card the
  first source row is +0x260; for other cards it is zero. The cursor y begins
  at card_y+1, or card_y+2 for a one-line description, then subtracts scroll
  and adds the source line index. pe-display-fields.tsv preserves the sites.

Ordered paragraph production and omitted branches
  1. If historical figure death_year(+0x30) != -1:
       Died in the year {signed-year}
     The source has no terminal period. The year uses the native signed
     integer formatter. -1 is omitted, not displayed.

  2. Known creature/type label. If the optional card+0x80 knowledge record
     has a race, use that race/caste label and capitalize it. Otherwise its
     historical figure ID is resolved: deity flag -> {creature-label} deity;
     force flag -> Force; missing record/unsupported flags -> no type row.
     Without a knowledge record, use the card figure's own deity/force/race
     branches. The creature supplier can return an empty label on invalid
     race data. The appended deity suffix can therefore be the entire row.

  3. Historical figure entity-link loop (all matching links, not one choice):
     Link type 13 resolves the linked military assignment's entity and
     position. Any missing link, entity, assignment or position omits that
     whole paragraph. Otherwise:
       This person is one of the {plural-position} of {entity}{suffix}.
     plural-position is the position string at +0x218, appended even when
     empty. suffix is selected in this priority order:
       linked assignment == adventurer commander assignment:
         " and your military subordinate"
       else linked assignment == adventurer own military assignment:
         " alongside you"
       else empty.
     The native string therefore permits "one of the  of ": this is a real
     empty dynamic position, not a different untranslated fixed message.

     Link type 10 resolves entity, assignment and position; absent source
     records omit the paragraph. Otherwise:
       This person is {gendered-position} of {owner}{suffix}.
     gendered-position comes from leaf 99a3c0(position,person.sex,0,0).
     It uses female/male strings when available, otherwise the base string.
     The journal does not add an English article; the returned string may
     be empty. The leaf also retains the unused-by-this-call adjective and
     plural branches, and all their native fallback paths.

     owner is usually the generated entity name. If position+0x2c8 > 0,
     9bdfb0 searches entity deity links: flags&0x200 and matching assignment
     position ID. A resolved deity historical figure appends " of " plus
     its generated figure name and returns true. False falls back to the
     entity supplier. Consequently this producer always has " of "; the
     religious success path supplies it itself. The owner may be empty if
     the generated name is empty. The entity supplier's unresolved-ID
     fallback is "an unknown civilization". Journal calls pass flags zero,
     so the supplier's optional LPAGE markup is not used by this producer.

     suffix is " and your military commander" only if the linked assignment
     commander is not -1 and equals the adventurer's military assignment;
     otherwise empty. The terminal period is always appended. Empty title
     and/or owner values retain their native surrounding spaces and period.

  4. Adventurer knowledge of the figure's birth:
       You have known this person your entire life.
       You have known this person since {her|his|its} birth.
       You have known each other your entire lives.
     These are mutually exclusive birth-year comparisons after the known
     figure/source record lookup succeeds. Missing records omit the group.

  5. If the last-conversation record resolves and its year != -1:
       You last spoke {relative-time}.
     The complete 22 native alternatives are preserved in the relative-time
     leaf and pe-literals.tsv: time-before-time, future, just-now, all elapsed
     minute/hour/day/week/month/year thresholds, and long/long-long-ago.

  6. If the adventurer guide recommendation lookup succeeds:
       You have heard this name suggested as a potential guide to faraway places.

  7. Adventurer direct relationship loop. Enum 4..15 maps to the twelve
     retained jump-table targets in pe-switches.tsv, in this order:
       4  You worship this figure.
       5  This is your lover.
       6  This is your prisoner.
       7  This is your jailor.
       8  This is your master.
       9  This is your apprentice.
       10 This is your traveling companion.
       11 This is your former master.
       12 This is your former apprentice.
       13 This is your owner.
       14 This is your former spouse.
       15 This is your deceased spouse.
     Other enum values, unmatched figure IDs and absent links emit no row.
     Worship can append exactly one suffix to the SAME paragraph, with two
     separating spaces, if the adventurer's divine-link state permits it:
       >=100 "  You are beloved."
       >=75  "  You are held in high regard."
       >=50  "  You are held in some esteem."
       >=25  "  You have been favorably noticed."
       >0    "  You have attracted some positive interest."
       <=0 or missing qualifying source record: no suffix.

  8. If bb2f30 resolves a family relation rather than -1:
       This is your {kinship}
     75a580 supplies the complete kinship enum and default. The producer
     wraps the string BEFORE appending its period to the temporary string;
     the actual paragraph has no terminal period. Both forms are covered by
     the shared grammar because other consumers can supply the period.

  9. In adventure game type 1, when the native adventurer eligibility flags
     allow social assessment, bc0f20 calculates the 31 reputation scores
     and bc360 appends their captions. This supplier emits no caption when
     all scores are <=0. Otherwise it inserts an empty row, "Reputation:",
     another empty row, then iterates selectors 0..30 in enum order. Each
     positive score emits a single capitalized label chosen by thresholds
     >=100, >=75, >=50, >=25, >0. It does not put blank rows between labels.
     The 155 exact resulting labels, selector numbers, thresholds and
     literal instruction sites are in pe-reputation-productions.tsv.

Runtime source correspondence
  data/runtime/adventure-journal-grammar.tsv journal-person owns complete
  position/membership paragraphs, nullable fields, military suffixes,
  birth/last-conversation/family forms and exact fixed message composition.
  journal-person-kind owns Force and deity/creature forms.
  Native complete paragraphs must be recovered from +0x68 cached rows before
  grammar translation, since names or position words can cross wrapped rows.
  Separate source paragraphs remain separated by the native empty rows.

  Relative times reuse all rumor-time branches. Kinship reuses the complete
  dialogue-family vocabulary. Fixed relationships, guide recommendations,
  lifelong familiarity, worship and all five regard sentences reuse
  data/runtime/ui-messages.tsv adventure.log entries through $message.
  Generated entity/person names reuse their typed existing name translation.
  Dynamic empty position strings receive a neutral membership translation,
  rather than requiring a nonexistent English position label.

  Reputation uses all 155 existing data/runtime/legends-events.tsv entries
  with the reputation category and the existing "Adventurer log reputation: "
  translation key. Its rows remain separate caption entries, rather than
  being concatenated into one fixed-prose paragraph. No custom squad.alias
  spelling is used to infer that a name should be translated.

Reproduction
  Run tools/extract_adventure_journal_people_pe.py with the fixed Windows
  Python interpreter. It reads the two configured original PEs through the
  fixed objdump.exe and emits only this offline extraction directory.
  The saved PE manifests are consumed by DecompileJournalAgreementsPE.java
  with arguments: this directory, then steam or classic. The local native
  Ghidra installation is dfcn-analysis-tools/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC and its
  configured JDK is dfcn-analysis-tools/jdk-25.0.4.1+1. Separate temporary
  application.settingsdir and application.cachedir avoid shared Felix state.
  These are reverse-engineering outputs, not build inputs or display claims.
